You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

What kind of “popularity” do you want to analyze (viewers, rating/share, weekly rank, or all of them), and do you want results **by series/channel** or **over time**?

Meanwhile, here are a few ready-to-run SQL queries commonly used for TV series popularity analysis with your schema.

### 1) Most popular episodes by viewers (top 20)
```sql
SELECT
  ts.Episode,
  ts.Air_Date,
  ts.Viewers_m,
  ts.Rating,
  ts.Share,
  ts.Weekly_Rank,
  ch.series_name AS channel_series_name,
  ch.id AS channel_id
FROM TV_series ts
LEFT JOIN TV_Channel ch ON ch.id = ts.Channel
WHERE ts.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CAST(ts.Viewers_m AS REAL) DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### 2) Best average weekly rank by channel (lower = better)
```sql
SELECT
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name,
  AVG(ts.Weekly_Rank) AS avg_weekly_rank,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count
FROM TV_series ts
JOIN TV_Channel ch ON ch.id = ts.Channel
WHERE ts.Weekly_Rank IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ch.id, ch.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_weekly_rank ASC;
```

### 3) Average viewers and rating by channel
```sql
SELECT
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name,
  AVG(CAST(ts.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  AVG(CAST(ts.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
  AVG(CAST(ts.Share AS REAL))  AS avg_share,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count
FROM TV_series ts
JOIN TV_Channel ch ON ch.id = ts.Channel
GROUP BY ch.id, ch.series_name
ORDER BY avg_viewers_m DESC;
```

### 4) Popularity trend over time (monthly average viewers)
```sql
SELECT
  substr(ts.Air_Date, 1, 7) AS month,
  AVG(CAST(ts.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  COUNT(*) AS episodes
FROM TV_series ts
WHERE ts.Air_Date IS NOT NULL
  AND ts.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY substr(ts.Air_Date, 1, 7)
ORDER BY month;
```

### 5) 18–49 performance (if stored like “1.2/4”)
This extracts rating/share from `18_49_Rating_Share` formatted as `rating/share`.
```sql
SELECT
  ch.id AS channel_id,
  ch.series_name,
  AVG(CAST(substr(ts."18_49_Rating_Share", 1, instr(ts."18_49_Rating_Share", '/') - 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_18_49_rating,
  AVG(CAST(substr(ts."18_49_Rating_Share", instr(ts."18_49_Rating_Share", '/') + 1) AS REAL)) AS avg_18_49_share,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count
FROM TV_series ts
JOIN TV_Channel ch ON ch.id = ts.Channel
WHERE ts."18_49_Rating_Share" LIKE '%/%'
GROUP BY ch.id, ch.series_name
ORDER BY avg_18_49_rating DESC;
```

1) which metric defines popularity for you (viewers vs rank vs rating),  
2) the time window (all time / a year / a date range), and  
3) whether you want by **channel**, **episode**, or **country/language**,

I want to identify the minimum share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MIN(CAST(Share AS REAL)) AS min_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
also need to find the maximum share of all TV series

```sql
SELECT
  MIN(CAST(Share AS REAL)) AS min_share,
  MAX(CAST(Share AS REAL)) AS max_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
